predecessors.name: British Colonial Empire
predecessors.text: British Guiana: 'In 1831, the united colonies of Demerara-Essequibo and separate colony of Berbice together became a single British colony'

ledger.x: 26 May 1966: British Guiana becomes independent Guyana.
October 1966: Venezuelan troops occupy Ankoko Island, five months after independence.
12 December 1967: Guyanese police land at Oronoque in the New River Triangle, which Suriname had occupied with posts.
1969: the Guyana Defence Force takes full control of the New River Triangle.
Still in force when the record ends: 'The island remains under Venezuelan administration, where a Venezuelan airport and a military base operate.'

wars.name: Ankoko occupation and Rupununi uprising (Essequibo dispute)
wars.outcome: Venezuela kept Ankoko Island; Guyana kept the rest of the land west of the Essequibo.

wars.name: Tigri Area (New River Triangle) clashes with Suriname
wars.outcome: Guyana seized full control in 1969; the November 1970 agreement to withdraw was not kept and Guyana still holds the Triangle, which Suriname claims.

wars.name: Essequibo crisis of 2023-2024
wars.outcome: No change on the ground: Venezuela held a referendum in December 2023 ('No vote was held in the disputed region') and in March 2024 passed a law designating Essequibo as a new Venezuelan state.
